hypothesis: For every cellular automaton tested and every block of n cells repeated forever as the initial condition, the evolution is eventually time-periodic with period at most k^n (k = number of colours; 2^n for two colours), and the infinite repeated-block configuration evolves exactly as a cyclic ring of n cells.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: (1) across all (rule, block) pairs enumerated, 100% have eventual temporal period <= k^n (zero violations); (2) for every (rule, block) pair in the equivalence sample, the central block of a long line made of repeated copies of the block evolves identically to the n-cell ring for all simulated steps (zero mismatching cells).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: any (rule, block) pair whose eventual period exceeds k^n, or any pair for which the repeated-block line evolution differs from the ring evolution inside the region unaffected by the line's ends.
interpretation: 'Initial conditions which consist just of a fixed block of cells repeated forever' is a spatially n-periodic configuration on the infinite line. 'Simple repetitive behavior' is read as eventual time-periodicity of the configuration, and the stated bound 2^n is read, following Wolfram's own reasoning and the assessors, as k^n for k colours (2^n in the two-colour case the text has in mind). 'Any cellular automaton' cannot be enumerated, so three families are tested: all 256 elementary rules exhaustively (n = 1..12), all 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic rules (n = 1..6, bound 3^n), and a fixed-seed random sample of 500 two-colour range-2 (5-neighbour) rules out of 2^32 (n = 1..10). The reduction 'each block evolves like a finite cyclic system' is tested separately by simulating the actual repeated-block line and comparing it with the ring.

datasets.name: All 256 ECA x all 2^n blocks of n = 1..12 cells repeated forever (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: elementary cellular automata, Wolfram rule numbering; a block of n cells repeated forever is simulated as an n-cell ring with periodic boundaries; every one of the 2^n blocks is used; eventual period from the functional graph of the ring's 2^n states

datasets.name: All 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic rules x all 3^n blocks of n = 1..6 cells (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: totalistic rules on colours {0,1,2}: new colour = digit s of the rule code written in base 3 (least significant digit = sum 0), where s = sum of the three neighbourhood colours in 0..6; Wolfram's code numbering from NKS p. 60; rings of n cells, all 3^n blocks

datasets.name: 500 random two-colour range-2 rules (5-cell neighbourhood, 2^32 rule space; numpy default_rng seed 20261031) x all 2^n blocks of n = 1..10 (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: range-2 binary rules: new colour = bit of the 32-bit rule number indexed by the 5-cell neighbourhood value 16*c[-2]+8*c[-1]+4*c[0]+2*c[1]+c[2]; rings of n cells with wrap-around

datasets.name: All 256 ECA x all blocks of n = 1..6 cells, repeated on a long line, compared with the ring (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: a line of (2*steps/n + 6) copies of the block with fixed white ends, evolved for steps = 2^n + 2^n (transient bound plus period bound); the central copy is compared cell-by-cell with the n-cell ring evolution at every step
datasets.role: tests the reduction of the repeated-block line to a finite cyclic system

method: analysis.py treats a block of n cells repeated forever as an n-cell ring, builds the ring's transition map on all k^n states for each rule and computes the eventual period of every state's orbit from the functional graph (cycle detection by in-degree peeling). Families: all 256 ECA for n = 1..12 (2,096,640 rule-block pairs), all 2187 three-colour totalistic rules for n = 1..6 (2,388,204 pairs, bound 3^n), and 500 seeded random range-2 binary rules for n = 1..10 (1,023,000 pairs). It then checks the reduction itself: for all 256 ECA and all 32,256 blocks of n = 1..6, a line of repeated copies of the block is evolved for 2*2^n steps and its central copy compared cell by cell with the ring evolution (15,845,376 cells). Run time about 18 s.

measured.unit: fraction of (rule, block) pairs whose eventual temporal period is <= k^n
measured.uncertainty: exact (exhaustive within each family; the range-2 family is a seeded sample of 500 of 2^32 rules)

caveats: The claim quantifies over all cellular automata; three rule families (one exhaustive over all 256 elementary rules, one exhaustive over all 2187 three-colour totalistic rules, one a 500-rule sample of range-2 rules) were tested, and the general statement rests on the finite-state argument that the line-vs-ring check confirms empirically for the elementary rules.

The bound k^n is attained only in degenerate cases (n = 1, rules that cycle through every state); for n >= 2 the overwhelming majority of periods are below k^n / 10 (see the histogram), so the bound is loose but never violated.
Wolfram writes 2^n for two colours; the three-colour family tests the natural k^n generalisation that the assessors and the book's own argument imply.
